title: Evidence for Earliest Olive-Oil Production in Submerged Settlements off the Carmel Coast, Israel
version: Journal of Archaeological Science 24(12), 1141–1150. Published article and figure in author-uploaded copies.
lineage: Original excavation and interpretation of Kfar Samir installations. The Fig. 5 underwater scene reappears in Galili et al. (2007) Fig. 3 and Rosenberg et al. (2023) Fig. 7a.

passages.note: In pit 6, crushed and whole olive stones and pulp were recovered in alternating layers with organic clay above pebbles. The fill also contained reed and straw fragments.

Fig. 5 labels the find as a woven reed fragment associated with olive stones. Matching the photographed features identifies the 1994 twig fragments later called KS 2. The discussion proposes pressing by analogy and separately discusses reeds and straw in pit 6.
